brief: Something to keep my sewing supplies tidy.

requirements.requirement: Keeps sewing supplies tidy, with separate places for different items
requirements.evidence: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3 has 3 sections for small items like bobbins and thread spools. bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full-div2 has 2 sections for things like scissors and the tape measure. bin:0,1,0~hex-bin-full is one open bin for fabric scraps or a pin cushion. The small corner bin notch:0#1,1#notch2 has 3 sections for needles, pins and buttons. That makes 9 spaces in all.
capOpenFaces added 10 solid end caps and lockJoints added 3 joint bolts. check_build: no rule errors, no parts colliding.
There are no sewing props in the catalogue. Stand-ins: a marker and a pen in the 3-section bin, a pen in the small corner bin, and a tape measure on the bench beside the build.

finish.summary:
I built a small sewing organiser from three hex bases set in a triangle. It has 9 storage spaces: 3 in one bin, 2 in a second bin, 1 open bin and 3 in a small bin in the corner where the bases meet. All open faces are capped and the joints are bolted. check_build found no rule errors and no parts colliding. 17 parts, about 1786 g of filament.

There are no sewing items in the prop catalogue, so I staged it with stand-ins instead: a marker and a pen standing in the 3-section bin, a pen in the small corner bin, and a tape measure on the bench beside it. A 300 mm ruler was too long for the 2-section bin, and the tape measure didn't fit in the open bin.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
